styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Great Siege Tunnels, the Upper Rock fortifications and the old town.

styles.label: Wildlife
styles.blurb: Barbary macaques, sea views and Upper Rock trails.

styles.label: Adventure
styles.blurb: Cable car rides, steep walks and cliff-top viewpoints.

stays.why: In the heart of the old town, steps from the Convent, Cathedral and Main Street shops. Best base for walking.
Quiet fishing village on the east side with a sandy beach and seafront bars. Taxi ride to the town centre.
Near the lighthouse, Europa Point mosque and Trafalgar Cemetery. Quieter, with sea views but fewer restaurants.
Marina hotels and restaurants close to the cruise port. Good for sunset walks and evening dining.

food: Try local Gibraltarian dishes such as calentita (chickpea flour cake) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew) in old-town restaurants.
Tapas bars along Main Street and Irish Town serve Spanish-style small plates. Share several to try more.
Fish and chips and pub meals are common near the marina and Ocean Village. Good for a relaxed dinner.
Bakeries and cafés in the old town sell cheap pastries and sandwiches for lunch on the go.
Many shops and cafés take card, but keep some small coins for buses. Prices are in pounds (£), so check menus before you order.
more_time: Spend a day in Spain: walk across the border from La Línea and take a local bus to nearby towns. Check bus times and border queues first.
Visit Gorham's Cave Complex on the Upper Rock, a UNESCO-listed Neanderthal site. Check opening days and tour times before you go.
Add a half-day for the Great Siege Tunnels and Trafalgar Cemetery. Both suit history fans and fit easily with a cable car trip.

recommend.why: Two nights give you time for the Upper Rock, the tunnels and a slow evening in the old town without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: Mild and wet, highs near 16°C and about 9 rainy days. Pack a light jacket and waterproofs.
Feb: Cool and damp, highs near 16°C with about 8 rainy days. Good for quiet museum visits.
Mar: Highs near 18°C and the wettest month at about 11 rain days. Bring an umbrella for the Upper Rock.
Apr: Pleasant, highs near 20°C with about 8 rain days. Good weather for walking and wildlife.
May: Warm and mostly dry, highs near 23°C with about 4 rain days. Ideal for outdoor sightseeing.
Jun: Hot and sunny, highs near 26°C with only about 2 rain days. Start walks early.
Jul: Hottest and driest, highs near 30°C with no rain days on average. Plan shade and water.
Aug: Hot and nearly dry, highs near 30°C with about 1 rain day. Keep outdoor walks short.
Sep: Still warm, highs near 27°C with about 5 rain days. Good for the Upper Rock after the heat eases.
Oct: Mild, highs near 23°C with about 8 rain days. A strong month for walking and sightseeing.
Nov: Cooler, highs near 19°C with about 8 rain days. Good for food and town walks.
Dec: Cool and damp, highs near 17°C with about 8 rain days. Pack layers for the Upper Rock wind.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Mediterranean climate: warm summers, cool damp winters and a lot of sun between spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: May to October
items.text: Highs of about 23–30°C and few rain days. Ideal for the Upper Rock and sea views.

items.title: Hot summers (July and August)
items.text: Highs near 30°C and lows around 21–22°C. Walk early or late and carry water.

items.title: Wettest in winter
items.text: December to March sees about 8–11 rain days per month. Carry a light waterproof jacket.

items.title: Windy on the Rock
items.text: The Upper Rock is exposed. Expect gusts on high paths, especially in winter.

items.title: Cool evenings
items.text: Lows drop to about 10–11°C in winter. Pack a warm layer for evenings out.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes for steep streets, sunscreen and a hat for summer, and a light jacket and umbrella for winter.

transit.best: Walk most of the old town and use taxis for the steep roads up to the Upper Rock.

modes.text: Gibraltar has no metro or tram. Don't plan around rail.
Citibus (routes 5 and 10) and Gibraltar Bus Company run the routes. Single fares start at £1.00 to £1.80 and are flat. Gibraltar Bus needs exact change or card; Citibus takes cash only.
Taxis are the easiest way up the steep roads. Check locally for ride-app coverage, as Uber is not reliably available.
Drive on the right. Much of the old centre has narrow one-way streets and very limited parking. Park in La Línea and walk across the border.
Walking covers most of the town. Wear comfortable shoes for steep, uneven streets.
A cable car links the town with the Upper Rock. Good for the top of the Rock without a steep climb.
